vignette: John, a 45-year-old male chef from Oceania, has been experiencing significant distress since a traumatic event that occurred several months ago. John was raped while working late one night at the restaurant where he is the head chef. The trauma of this event has left him struggling with intrusive memories and a deep sense of contamination and loss. Since the incident, John finds himself easily able to talk about what happened when prompted, but often struggles to put the memories in the correct sequence or to fully recall all details without feeling overwhelmed by intense emotions that force him to push the memory away. This inability to form coherent recollections has contributed to his sense of helplessness and despair. John’s experience at work now feels tainted by this event. He no longer finds joy in cooking, which was once a source of pride and identity for him. His negative appraisals about himself have significantly impacted how he perceives the memories. He is certain that his life has been irrevocably destroyed because of what happened, and as a result, he feels contaminated by the trauma. This contamination makes it hard for him to fully engage with the memory without feeling dirtied again. These negative appraisals have also led John to question his own capabilities. He fears that he can no longer handle the pressure or responsibilities associated with being a chef. Consequently, he avoids going over details of the incident at work, as even discussing it there makes him feel increasingly isolated from colleagues who do not understand what he is going through. John’s negative appraisals have further influenced his memory process by reinforcing his tendency to avoid fully engaging with and completing the recollection of the event. When he starts to recall parts of the trauma, he often feels overwhelmed and pushes the memory away before it is complete, exacerbating his sense of being unable to cope and making him feel like his life has been completely ruined. The trauma has not only affected John’s work but also his personal life. He has become increasingly isolated since the divorce from his ex-wife, as he finds it difficult to form new relationships due to his deep-seated beliefs that he is no longer capable of being a whole person. This isolation adds another layer of distress and reinforces his negative appraisals. John’s current state is one of profound despair and fear. He finally sought help after realizing that his work performance was declining, leading to conflicts with the restaurant owner who had started questioning his competence. His primary concern now is finding a way to regain some semblance of normalcy in his life and not feeling like he is living under a constant cloud of contamination and failure. What frightens John most is the possibility that he will never be able to reclaim his identity as a chef or find peace with what happened. However, there is also hope; he hopes that through therapy, he can begin to address these negative appraisals and work towards integrating the fragmented memories without feeling overwhelmed by the sense of contamination and loss. John’s journey now involves grappling with these deeply ingrained beliefs and memories, seeking a path forward where he can reclaim his life and identity.
